title: 2018 AMC 10B Problem 6
statement: A box contains \(5\) chips, numbered \(1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(4,\) and \(5.\) Chips are drawn randomly one at a time without replacement until the sum of the values drawn exceeds \(4.\) What is the probability that \(3\) draws are required?

solutions.text:
We need a third draw exactly when the first two chips still sum to \(4\) or less. The only such unordered pairs are \(\{1,2\}\) and \(\{1,3\}.\) Each can be drawn in either order, giving \(4\) favorable ordered prefixes.

Imagine that a complete random ordering of all five chips is chosen in advance. Then all \(5\cdot4=20\) ordered first-two-chip prefixes are equally likely, even when the actual process would stop after the first chip. Thus the probability is \(\frac{4}{20}=\frac{1}{5}.\) Therefore, the answer is D.
hints: A third draw is needed exactly when the first two chips still sum to at most \(4\)
Which pairs of distinct chips sum to \(4\) or less? Count them among all ordered first-two-draw outcomes
